records_read.citation: Abrao J, Fernandes CR, White PF, Shimano AC, Okubo R, Lima GB, Bachur JA, Garcia SB. Effect of local anaesthetic infiltration with bupivacaine and ropivacaine on wound healing: a placebo-controlled study. Int Wound J 2014;11:379-385
records_read.matches: The rat wound study the page is describing: 72 rats, randomised double-blind infiltration with saline, bupivacaine or ropivacaine before a standardised incision, with histochemistry and mechanical testing on day 3 and day 14.
records_read.misses: The histological endpoints are macrophage count, transforming growth factor beta-1, collagen and CD34; innervation and nerve fibre density are not among them.

records_read.citation: Zarucco L, Driessen B, Scandella M, Cozzi F, Cantile C. Sensory nerve conduction and nociception in the equine lower forelimb during perineural bupivacaine infusion along the palmar nerves. Can J Vet Res 2010;74:305-313
records_read.matches: The nearest study of prolonged local-anaesthetic exposure with a nerve endpoint: continuous perineural bupivacaine infusion over six days in horses against saline in the contralateral limb, with sensory nerve conduction velocity measured to detect nerve injury and myelinated fibre morphometry performed on palmar nerve specimens.
records_read.misses: Perineural catheter rather than wound infiltration; the morphometry characterises fibre distribution in separate animals rather than measuring the effect of the infusion, and the infusion endpoint is conduction velocity, not innervation density.

records_read.citation: Wehrfritz A, Namer B, Ihmsen H, Mueller C, Filitz J, Koppert W, Leffler A. Differential effects on sensory functions and measures of epidermal nerve fiber density after application of a lidocaine patch (5%) on healthy human skin. Eur J Pain 2011;15:907-912
records_read.matches: A study of prolonged local-anaesthetic exposure that does measure innervation: randomised double-blind, healthy volunteers, six weeks of patch against placebo patch, epidermal nerve fibre density in skin blister roofs.
records_read.misses: Topical patch on intact skin rather than continuous infiltration of an incised wound, so it sits outside the sub-literature this sentence is about; the page cites it separately in 6.7.

records_read.citation: Richard BM, Ott LR, Haan D, Brubaker AN, Cole PI, Nelson KG, Ross PE, Rebelatto MC, Newton PE. The safety and tolerability evaluation of DepoFoam bupivacaine administered by incision wound infiltration in rabbits and dogs. Expert Opin Investig Drugs 2011;20:1327-1341
records_read.matches: Incision wound infiltration in two species with histology at day 3 and day 15 and wound-healing follow-up.
records_read.misses: Histology of the surgical site and wound healing; no innervation or nerve fibre endpoint.

quote: A moderate but significant decrease in epidermal nerve fiber density was observed in skin blister roofs obtained after 42days of treatment with lidocaine patches.
proposed_wording: Within the continuous wound-infiltration literature, searches of Europe PMC and of an earlier worker's PubMed searches through October 2026 found no study with an innervation or nerve-fibre-density endpoint; prolonged local-anaesthetic exposure has been studied with an innervation endpoint by another route in humans (Wehrfritz 2011, PMID 21530339) and with nerve conduction and fibre morphometry during six-day perineural infusion in horses (Zarucco 2010, PMID 21197231).
reason: Judged inside the bullet's own scope - continuous infiltration of incised subcutaneous tissue - the claim holds: the rat wound study and the animal wound-infiltration safety work measure inflammatory, collagen, vascular and healing endpoints, never innervation. As a bare sentence 'no study measures innervation' is too broad, because the page's own 6.7 cites a human study of six weeks' local-anaesthetic exposure that counted epidermal nerve fibres, and Zarucco 2010 measured nerve conduction after six days of perineural infusion. Adding 'in this literature' or 'in the wound-infiltration studies' makes it exact.

records_read.citation: Dias MP, Newton DJ, McLeod GA, Khan F, Belch JJ. The inhibitory effects of local anaesthetics on the vascular flare responses to bradykinin and substance P in human skin. Anaesthesia 2008;63:151-155
records_read.matches: Isolates the drug-suppressed-flare term on its own in human skin, and does it for ropivacaine among three agents: cutaneous flare responses to intradermal bradykinin and substance P measured with and without lidocaine, levobupivacaine and ropivacaine, all three significantly attenuating the responses.
records_read.misses: The flare is provoked by an injected mediator rather than by the wheal's own needle, so the drug term is separated from a different flare, not from the needle-created one.

records_read.citation: Forster C, Greiner T, Nischik M, Schmelz M, Handwerker HO. Neurogenic flare responses are heterogeneous in superficial and deep layers of human skin. Neurosci Lett 1995;185:33-36
records_read.matches: Human skin, histamine-provoked neurogenic flare measured by infrared thermography and video image analysis, with the visible flare suppressed by a topically applied local anaesthetic while the warming reaction was not.
records_read.misses: Topical anaesthetic and a histamine-provoked flare, so again not the needle's own flare.

records_read.citation: Kawamata M, Takahashi T, Kozuka Y, Nawa Y, Nishikawa K, Narimatsu E, Watanabe H, Namiki A. Experimental incision-induced pain in human skin: effects of systemic lidocaine on flare formation and hyperalgesia. Pain 2002;100:77-89
records_read.matches: Comes closest to separating a drug's flare suppression from a trauma-created flare in humans: a standardised forearm incision with flare measured by laser Doppler imager, and lidocaine given systemically before or after the incision.
records_read.misses: Systemic lidocaine, not a wheal, so there is no needle-borne drug delivery and no wheal flare to separate.

records_read.citation: Cederholm I, Evers H, Lofstrom JB. Effect of intradermal injection of saline or a local anaesthetic agent on skin blood flow - a methodological study in man. Acta Anaesthesiol Scand 1991;35:208-215
records_read.matches: The one wheal study with the controls that would be needed: needle-insertion-only and saline arms beside the drug arms, by laser Doppler.
records_read.misses: Measures skin blood flow at the injected site from 20 min onward, not the axon-reflex flare and its suppression, so the third term is not separated.

quote: Skin blood flow responses to intradermal injections of bradykinin and substance P were assessed in the absence and presence of anaesthetic and analgesic concentrations of lidocaine, levobupivacaine and ropivacaine.
proposed_wording: No study was found that separates a local anaesthetic's suppression of the flare from the flare its own needle creates in the same wheal; the suppression term alone has been measured in human skin for ropivacaine and two other agents against mediator-provoked flare (Dias 2008, PMID 18211446), for a topical anaesthetic against histamine-provoked flare (Forster 1995, PMID 7731549), and for systemic lidocaine against incision-induced flare (Kawamata 2002, PMID 12435461).
reason: Within the claim's intervention element - a local anaesthetic wheal - nothing found separates the drug's flare suppression from the needle's own flare, and Cederholm 1991 has the needle-only and saline controls but measures blood flow rather than the axon-reflex flare. The claim is too broad in calling it a term nobody has separated, since the suppression term has been isolated in human skin, including for ropivacaine, by provoking the flare with an independent stimulus. The page's convention at 0.1 already scopes its negatives as search-limited, so this is a wording correction: nobody has separated it within a wheal.
